On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 12:18, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karthik — looped you in for a fast triage.

Team — quick triage notes (prelim):
1) Observed symptom: simultaneous latency p95 increase and 503s originating from the inference layer's batching worker pool. Telemetry shows a backlog of small requests that collated into larger batches; when the batch size hit a threshold near 2x expected, the KV cache warmup combined with kernel path for quantized ops led to increased GC/CPU contention and transient OOMs on one GPU slot. That cascaded into 503s while autoscaler attempted to reassign pods.
2) Trigger: a client pattern change amplified by our recent batching heuristic tweak (rolled quietly at 11:45 UTC). The heuristic change increased aggressive batching for short inputs — that interaction created pathological batches for a high-rps client.
3) Mitigation enacted at 15:10 UTC: we pushed a rollback of the batching heuristic to stable (hotfix) and disabled aggressive coalescing for the affected pool. Initial canary shows error rate back to baseline and p95 moving toward normal.
4) Next steps (short): collect full heap traces from the effected node, widen canary to prod subset, run a backfill to confirm regression fixed.

I've attached preliminary RCA notes and the canary deploy details. Will follow with a full writeup.

Attachments: [attachment: prelim-rca-notes.pdf (120KB)]

—Karthik

Subject: OrchardBay — RCA summary and remediation tracker (deliverable)

Samir / Claire / OrchardBay team — thanks again for patience while we validated the mitigation. Below is an executive-style RCA summary plus the corrective action tracker. We'll publish a full technical packet (detailed heap traces, replay, test harness) to the drive link in the morning.

Executive RCA (summary):
- What happened: A recent batching heuristic change (11:45 UTC) caused pathological coalescing for a high-RPS client pattern, producing oversized batches that hit an untested kernel execution path for our quantized model variant. The oversized batches increased memory pressure and triggered transient OOMs, which led to 503 responses while the autoscaler recovered slot assignments.
- Why it impacted OrchardBay: OrchardBay's checkout traffic has a consistent short-input, high-frequency pattern that amplified the heuristic effect. Their traffic density meant the failure mode produced visible SLO breaches.
- Immediate mitigation: Rolled back the heuristic and disabled aggressive coalescing for the affected pool (15:10 UTC). Canary (30%) validated recovery; full rollout paused until validation completes.

Corrective action tracker (owners + ETA):
- Action 1: Add a dedicated unit/integration test for batching-edge cases + simulated OrchardBay pattern. Owner: Karthik Iyer. ETA: 2027-07-07.
- Action 2: Implement per-customer batching-safety knobs (config flag to opt-out of aggressive coalescing). Owner: Jonas Weber. ETA: 2027-07-14.
- Action 3: Post-deploy monitoring rule to alarm on batch-size distribution skew + automatic rollback. Owner: Mina Haddad. ETA: 2027-07-05.
- Action 4: Credit calculation and formal SLO impact packet for OrchardBay. Owner: Marissa Cole. ETA: 2027-07-01.
- Action 5: Run a controlled replay test and publish kernel-level traces to the incident drive. Owner: Karthik Iyer. ETA: 2027-07-03.

Attachments (sent): [attachment: prelim-rca-notes.pdf], [attachment: orchardbay_request_logs_20270630.zip], [attachment: orchardbay-slo-impact-summary.csv]

We will run a joint postmortem readout at 09:30 US PST tomorrow (Thu) — meeting invite to follow. If OrchardBay needs a faster executive note for finance, Marissa will push the credit estimate by EOD.

Thanks — Mina
